newsitem.title: UK: London PGM price rise to continue, gold in range.
newsitem.headline: London PGM price rise to continue, gold in range.

text.p: Platinum group metals (PGM) prices were forecast to continue the firmer trend seen for most of this month on Friday, despite Russia making its first platinum delivery of the year to Tokyo overnight.
But gold and silver prices were expected to remain in a narrow range following a volatile ending to New York's trading session on Thursday, traders said.
The platinum and palladium markets have been increasingly short of metal since administrative problems snagged Russian exports of the metals in December last year.
Russia is the world's largest palladium exporter and the second largest supplier of platinum after South Africa.

Platinum was fixed at $421.00 per ounce, up $4.00, and palladium at $201.00, up $3.00, as they continued a steady climb that began when the first Russian deliveries of the year failed to arrive as expected earlier this month.
"This isn't over by a long way," one dealer said.
"As long as lease rates remain high and the market stays tight the high prices will go on," he added.
The dealer said buying was coming in from industrial users who had previously leased platinum and palladium for use as process catalysts that would be returned to dealers for re-refining when spent.
"They are now faced with the prospect of costly rollovers or outright purchases of metal," the dealer said.

One-month borrowing rates for palladium were quoted at around 80 percent on Friday, with platinum at 35 percent. Longer-term rates were around 55 and 25 percent respectively, which was also unprecedented, the dealer said.
Ironically the extreme market tightness meant that few Russian offers to sell metal to dealers in Europe had been accepted.
"When you are talking about borrowing rates of over 80 percent and Russia can't deliver for two weeks, it is very expensive to finance that sort of purchase," he said.
Platinum fixed at its highest in seven years at $495 last month and palladium reached a 17-year peak of $240 when the market's tightness was at its peak.
Gold fixed firmer at $324.50 per ounce from $321.95 on Thursday, spurred by a volatile close in New York.
Dealers said gold should remain in a $323-$325 range on Friday. "It is still a sell-the-rally market," a dealer said.
Silver was indicated at $4.30/$4.32, up a cent and likely to be confined to a $425-$4.35 range.
